chunks: If God sends you harm, there is no one but He who can take it away; and if He bring you good, surely He has power over everything.

key_terms.يَمْسَسْکَ: touches or affects you (with harm or good)

ai.seo_question: Who is the only one who can remove harm and bring good according to the Quran?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse is often cited to illustrate the concept of *Tawhid al-Af'al* (Oneness of Divine Action), affirming that all occurrences of harm and good ultimately stem from God's will, though He is not the author of evil in a moral sense. It serves as a foundational text for understanding divine decree (*Qadr*) and encourages believers to maintain hope in God's capacity to remove distress, as seen in the supplications of the Ahl al-Bayt.
